pipeline_name: Badr El Din Spur Gas Pipelines

validity.recommendation: Do not treat as an operating gas transmission pipeline. The 16-in/130/Abu Sennan spec traces to a PROPOSED CO2-EOR transport concept, not a built line. Recommend: (a) verify whether any real Badr El Din / Abu Sennan gas line exists and its true specs; if none confirmable, flag for removal or reclassify status away from 'operating'; (b) treat P3938 as a likely duplicate/artifact of sibling P3937 (same wiki page, endpoints, 130 length, owner) pending confirmation the two are physically distinct pipes; (c) if any real line is confirmed, correct length (source figure is 130 MILES ~209 km, GEM recorded 130 km) and re-source the 150 MMcf/d capacity, which is unsupported.
validity.researcher_notes: P3938 is the '(2)' segment of a two-row 'Badr El Din Spur Gas Pipelines' wiki entry (sibling P3937 = 'Badr El Din Spur (1)'). Both rows share ONE citation: the egyptoil-gas.com 'The Western Desert' overview PDF (March 2015 Egypt Oil & Gas special report). That PDF is a graphics-heavy regional overview whose text is not machine-extractable and does NOT name any 'Badr El Din Spur' pipeline or give any 16-in/130/150 MMcf/d spec — a generic citation that does not name this line, i.e. an existence flag on its own. EXISTENCE: The only independent trace of a '16-inch pipeline to Abu Sennan, 130' is a PROPOSED CO2-EOR concept in Oil & Gas Journal (Cairo University Petroleum & Petrochemical Consultation Group authors): 'The CO2-rich gas streams can be gathered from the four plants to a central point in the El Salam area, then transported via 130-mile, 16-in. pipeline to Abu Sennan field to be stored in order to fulfill the EOR project's needs.' OGJ explicitly frames it as a concept the authors were 'trying to push,' not a built asset. This matches P3938's 16-in diameter, Abu Sennan endpoint, and '130' length exactly. So P3938's status='operating' is almost certainly wrong (proposal, not operating), and the length '130 km' is a units error for '130 miles' (~209 km). CLASSIFICATION: even if built, the OGJ line carries CO2-rich gas (~70% CO2, ~51.2 MMscfd available) for EOR/storage — a CO2 injection line, not a natural-gas transmission trunk. SPEC: capacity 150 MMcf/d is unsupported by any source found (the CO2 volume available is 51.2 MMscfd). ATTRIBUTION cross-check: Abu Sennan concession is operated by Kuwait Energy Egypt / United Energy Group (nsenergybusiness), producing only ~3.5 MMcf/d gas as of 2020 — wholly inconsistent with a 150 MMcf/d, 130 km, 16-in transmission spur terminating there; the GEM owner 'General Petroleum Co' (GPC) matches only a small GPC gas/condensate PLANT at Abu Sennan (~85 MMcf/d), not a long trunk. No independent source (English or trade) confirms an operating 16-in Badr El Din -> Abu Sennan gas transmission pipeline of these dimensions. DUPLICATE: P3937 (20-in/180) carries identical endpoints, 130 length, and owner on the same wiki page; the pair looks like one conceptual line arbitrarily split by diameter rather than two verified physical pipes.

routes.start_name: Badr El Din / El Salam field cluster (Abu Gharadig basin, northern Western Desert)
routes.end_name: Abu Sennan field, Western Desert, Egypt
routes.corridor_desc: Existence is in doubt (see validity), so a route is premature. IF any line exists along this corridor, the OGJ CO2-EOR concept describes CO2-rich gas gathered from four Western Desert plants (Obaiyed, El Salam, Tarek, El Qasr) to a central point in the El Salam area, then a 130-mile line to the Abu Sennan field. All named places sit in the Abu Gharadig basin of the northern Western Desert, administratively spanning Matruh governorate, roughly between ~29.5-30.2 N and ~27.5-28.5 E. I do not have a defensible point geocode for the individual fields, so lat/lon are left null rather than fabricated; the bound is loose (basin-scale, ~1 degree box). Corridor runs generally west/northwest (El Salam/Obaiyed area) to east (Abu Sennan) across the Abu Gharadig oil/gas province.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints named from the OGJ CO2-EOR paper (El Salam gathering point -> Abu Sennan field) and GEM's own Start=Badr El Din Field. No point coordinates fabricated; only the basin-scale corridor is defensible from the named Abu Gharadig-basin fields. Route suggestion is contingent on the pipeline actually existing, which this audit disputes.

summary: P3938 (Badr El Din Spur (2)) is a likely PHANTOM: sole citation is a generic PDF; its 16-in/130/Abu Sennan spec traces to a PROPOSED CO2-EOR concept (OGJ), status 'operating' unsupported, length '130 km' is really 130 miles, capacity 150 MMcf/d unsourced, and it duplicates sibling P3937.
